gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is omission of the input norm when estimating the action of (I-P_N)F on x in a local ball. ISSUE-002 instead diagnoses an invalid product approximation bound involving coefficient and branch errors; it does not recognize the missing ||x|| factor or the operator acting on x.

Both identify the invalid transfer from H^s-continuity plus C-compactness or compact Sobolev embedding to the C-topology continuity required by point-sampling approximation. Both recognize that this invalidates the functional and operator approximation claims and require a genuinely C-continuous premise or an appropriate stronger compactness assumption.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The approximation arguments require continuity in the input supremum topology, but H^s-continuity together with C-compactness and the compact embedding does not supply that continuity; consequently point-sampling neural approximants need not uniformly approximate the stated maps.

component_coverage.gold_component: The functional and operator approximation theorems incorrectly use H^s-continuity and C-compactness as if they supplied the required C-supremum continuity, so continuous point-sampling architectures cannot uniformly approximate all allowed maps.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly identifies the mismatch between H^s-continuity and the C topology required by the Chen-Chen approximation theorems, gives the corresponding C-compact counterexample, and proposes the needed C-continuity or H^s-compactness repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the missing domain-preservation conditions B_r(x*) subset D(F) and M_xi(B_r(x*)) subset D(F), without which F[M_xi x] is undefined. ISSUE-005 concerns zero extension, boundary layers, and the mollification rate, and does not diagnose domain membership or definedness of F on smoothed inputs.

The gold defect is the false same-radius localization claim M_xi(B_r(x*)) subset B_r(x*), caused by controlling distance from zero rather than distance from x*. ISSUE-005 instead diagnoses boundary artifacts and an incorrect mollification convergence rate; it does not recognize the failed neighborhood inclusion or the need for nested balls.

The gold issue is a quantifier-order error requiring one network to work simultaneously for every center, whereas the proof only constructs center-dependent local data. ISSUE-005 discusses boundary-induced mollification rates and does not address the quantifier order, simultaneous global approximation, or center dependence.
